newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM sees EMU decision soon.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM sees EMU decision soon.

text.p: Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said on Sunday his Social Democratic Party (SDP) would take a decision in June on Swedish membership of the European Union's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
Persson told reporters during a visit to the town of Fagersta that an SDP commission set up to make a recommendation on EMU membership would report its findings in the middle of May.
The party leadership would take a decision on membership in June, when it is dealing with recommendations to the party's annual congress, due to be held in September.
The full party would vote on the leadership's recommendation at the congress.
Opinion polls have consistently shown Swedes are against EMU and that social democrats make up the strongest anti-monetary union group. Sweden joined the EU in 1996.
Persson, an avowed supporter of monetary union in the past, has called for a full public debate in Sweden before any decision is taken.
